learningObjective: Compare NVLink and PCIe bandwidth for inter-GPU communication and reason about ring-AllReduce throughput.

canonicalClaims.claim: For bandwidth-bound ring-AllReduce, wall time scales inversely with the slowest inter-GPU link bandwidth; NVLink typically delivers an order of magnitude more per-direction bandwidth than PCIe on modern platforms, translating directly into collective speedup.
conditions: Tensor is large enough that latency terms are negligible.
Topology is fully connected via the compared interconnect; no fallback to PCIe or CPU routing.
Comparison is at steady state, not small-message regime.
nonImplications: Does not imply latency-bound collectives (small messages) show the same speedup.
Does not imply NVLink always solves all-to-all patterns; different collective algorithms use topology differently.

misconceptions.claim: Ring-AllReduce time is independent of link bandwidth.
misconceptions.whyWrong: In the bandwidth-bound regime, time = bytes / effective_link_BW; slower links directly increase time.
misconceptions.sourceOrEvidence: Standard collective analysis, e.g., NCCL and HP6

misconceptions.claim: CPU-mediated PCIe routing outperforms NVLink for large tensors.
misconceptions.whyWrong: CPU-mediated routing adds copies and involves lower-bandwidth links; NVLink is a direct GPU-to-GPU high-bandwidth fabric.

misconceptions.claim: NVLink and PCIe have the same per-direction bandwidth, differing only in aggregate.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Per-direction NVLink 4.0 is ~450 GB/s aggregate per GPU vs ~25 GB/s per direction on PCIe Gen4 x16; they differ by more than 10× per direction.

implementationFacts: NCCL ring-AllReduce bandwidth-bound time ≈ 2(P−1)/P × N / effective_link_BW.
PCIe Gen4 x16 ≈ 25 GB/s practical per direction.
performanceScenarios: Training LLMs on multi-node clusters uses NVLink/NVSwitch to hide gradient AllReduce behind backward pass; PCIe-only clusters see collective as a bottleneck.
